# Test fixtures

The `.h5` files are generated test data, not third-party datasets. Tests read
the committed files and do not require Python or a native HDF5 installation.

## Group storage regression fixture

Regenerate `group_storage.h5` from the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m venv /tmp/moon-hdf5-fixtures
/tmp/moon-hdf5-fixtures/bin/pip install h5py==3.16.0 numpy==2.5.4
/tmp/moon-hdf5-fixtures/bin/python scripts/generate_group_fixtures.py
```

The script fixes the HDF5 format bounds to v108 and verifies every dataset
with h5py after reopening the file. Object timestamps may vary on regeneration;
the regression tests compare structure and values rather than binary hashes.

| Path | Expected contents | MoonBit behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/empty` | No links | Return an empty link array |
| `/compact`, `/compact_ordered` | Two datasets each | Read both links and values |
| `/dense`, `/dense_ordered` | Twelve datasets each | Raise `UnsupportedFeature` when reading links |

Ordered groups track and index link creation order. Each dataset `value_NN`
contains two int32 values, `[NN, NN + 100]`. Twelve links exceed the default
compact group threshold and exercise dense storage with and without the
optional creation-order fields. Traversal and lookup through dense groups must
also report the unsupported feature, rather than silently omit their children.

The other fixtures predate this generator and are not regenerated by it.

## Chunk fill regression fixtures

Using the same Python environment, run:

```sh
/tmp/moon-hdf5-fixtures/bin/python scripts/generate_fill_fixtures.py
```

This regenerates `fill_v2.h5` (earliest/v108 format bounds) and `fill_v3.h5`
(v108/v108 bounds). Both use v1 chunk B-trees; the fill messages exercise v2
and v3. The script reopens each file and compares every value against NumPy.

`/numbers/signed`, `/numbers/big_endian`, `/numbers/floating`, and `/other/text`
have shape `(3, 5)` and chunks `(2, 3)`. Only two of four chunks are allocated.
Fill values are respectively -7, -1234, 1.5, and `none`; positions `(0, 0)`
and `(2, 4)` contain 42/99 or `yes`/`end`. `/other/unallocated` contains four
-9 values without allocated storage, `/other/default` contains four default
zeros, and `/other/partial_default` contains `[5, 0, 0, 0]`.

The fixture uses small groups to isolate fill behavior. During development,
placing all seven datasets directly in a v108 root group exposed a separate
object-header/traversal EOF issue; that compatibility issue remains unresolved.
